title: Quentin and the Witness
premise: August Thackeray, a night dispatcher who has spent three years cataloguing the town's secrets to stay invisible, receives a prepaid booking from a nervous client asking to be driven somewhere 'before it happens.' When the client is found alive but a stranger is dead in the exact spot, August realizes someone staged a murder that hasn't occurred yet — and that their own dispatch logs contain the killer's timeline. Partnering with Quentin, a disgraced ex-detective turned cab driver, August must decode their own files while dodging a killer who reads their records like scripture. In the end, August chooses justice outside the law, baiting the killer into confessing on an open dispatch channel, and Quentin chooses love over reinstatement, burning his testimony to keep August safe.
about_author: Juniper Reyes is a former small-town radio operator who spent a decade listening to strangers' voices in the dark before turning those nights into fiction. She writes mysteries about ordinary people who know too much and say too little.

chapters.title: The Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: POV: August. On a rain-slicked Tuesday shift, August takes an unusual prepaid booking from a trembling voice calling itself 'Wren,' requesting a 3 a.m. pickup at Hollow Bridge. The emotional beat is unease — August's instinct for anomalies pricks, and against all rules of staying invisible, they note the call in the log anyway.

chapters.title: A Murder That Hasn't Happened
chapters.summary: POV: August. At Hollow Bridge, Wren never appears; instead police swarm around a body that matches no missing-person file. August recognizes details from their own archived dispatch notes. The beat is dread: the crime scene feels rehearsed, as if someone performed a script August unknowingly wrote.

chapters.title: Quentin's Last Route
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Ex-detective Quentin Hale, now driving nights to outrun his old case failures, picks up August's flagged fare and finds Wren's burner phone taped under the seat. The beat is reluctant alliance — Quentin wants to hand it to the police; August knows exactly which cop is compromised.

chapters.title: Filed and Alphabetized
chapters.summary: POV: August. August walks Quentin through three years of dispatch archives, revealing how the town's secrets — affairs, bribes, a covered-up drowning — are encoded in routine call logs. They discover Wren's calls echo a pattern from a cold case. The beat is vertigo: August's survival system has become the killer's blueprint.

chapters.title: The Second Booking
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Another prepaid request arrives, this time naming Quentin as driver and August as passenger — a trap or an invitation. They follow it to an abandoned depot where they find Wren alive, hiding: a witness to the original drowning whose testimony was buried. The beat is fear sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Chief Knew
chapters.summary: POV: August. August confronts the compromised officer, Detective Marsh, using archived leverage to buy time, but realizes Marsh is being manipulated too — the killer is feeding him a false suspect. The beat is moral cost: August must spend a secret they swore never to spend, and someone gets hurt because of it.

chapters.title: Static on the Line
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. The killer contacts them through the dispatch channel itself, reciting August's logs verbatim, proving total surveillance of the taxi company. Wren is taken during the exchange. The beat is helplessness curdling into fury — and the first unguarded moment between August and Quentin, love admitted mid-crisis.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal
chapters.summary: POV: August. Decoding the killer's pattern, August realizes every 'impossible' detail mirrors the original drowning — the killer is restaging it with Wren as the victim, at Hollow Bridge, at 3 a.m., within forty-eight hours. The beat is grim clarity: the only way in is to play the role the script assigns.

chapters.title: Hollow Bridge, 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: POV: Quentin. Climax. August broadcasts a fabricated dispatch narrative luring the killer — the town's former coroner who faked the drowning report — into revealing himself on an open channel while Quentin intercepts him at the bridge with Wren. Violence flares; Quentin takes a knife wound protecting August. The beat is terror transfigured into defiance.

chapters.title: Off the Record
chapters.summary: POV: August. Resolution. The confession tape forces arrests, but August deletes the archive rather than let it testify against the town's small sinners, choosing mercy over completeness. Quentin declines reinstatement, keeping the truth of who baited the killer off the record. The beat is quiet peace: two people finally visible to each other, invisible to everyone else.
